# Remaining mount/nsenter caller assessment

Read-only assessment dated 2026-09-10. The accompanying JSON revalidates all 19 exact component/PURL/version/severity/CVE tuples against the SHA-bound retained reports. **Seven support narrowly scoped current-use exclusions; twelve remain unresolved and should not be waived. No application impact is confirmed.** No policy or repository files changed.

| CVE | Exact affected rows reviewed | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-53613 | Frontend WebUI/Admin UI `mount`, `libmount1`, 2.38.1-5+deb12u3: 4 | Scoped current frontend non-applicability |
| 2026-78408 | App/worker/audio-worker `util-linux`, 2.41.5-0+deb13u1: 3 | Scoped current firstparty caller non-applicability |
| 2026-76642 | App/worker/audio-worker `mount`, `libmount1`, 2.41.5-0+deb13u1: 6 | Unresolved local privilege boundary; keep gated |
| 2026-78410 | App/worker/audio-worker `mount`, `libmount1`, 2.41.5-0+deb13u1: 6 | Unresolved local privilege boundary; keep gated |

The exact tuples and reopening conditions are in `remaining-caller-review.json`. These are not additional absent-code dispositions.

## Concrete caller and permission evidence

- Exact Debian package payloads were retrieved without installation or execution and verified against the retained official security package index. `mount` archive SHA256 `eb70a615114ac40123768beb20e302554d5cb7edb33290be7e418ebe1075c878` contains `/usr/bin/mount` and `umount` owned by root with mode 4755. `util-linux` archive SHA256 `7d5b1176cc3d8cc6b290b3ec17af458f362d9200845f30da22057a8198744430` contains root-owned `nsenter` mode 0755. Backend OCI base bytes are unavailable: these are verified package payload permissions, not a measured final-image stat. See `caller-package-downloads.json` and `caller-deb-permissions.json`.
- The retained frontend base was independently rehashed: blob `a8ac7f6c67abc236e4c745052c404112b8fab6fe8ac3a329d1ef3b867ad67c71`, DiffID `1d69a5fd31932841d7825ef4780c06f008eea65aaa9f3110fe09d5832ed5c7d8`. Its root-owned mount is 4755. Its root-owned 0644 `/etc/fstab` contains only `# UNCONFIGURED FSTAB FOR BASE SYSTEM`. Runtime Dockerfiles preserve those paths and launch standalone Node servers: `Dockerfiles/Dockerfile.webui:56-84`, `Dockerfiles/Dockerfile.admin-ui:47-75`. No firstparty frontend child-process call was found. See `caller-frontend-base-proof.json`.
- Source searches cover Python application, frontend/Admin UI, entrypoints and helpers, excluding dependencies, tests and restricted branches. There are no direct `nsenter`, `--join-cgroup`, `X-mount.*`, libmount context, GVolume mount or `/etc/fstab` callers. Two quoted `mount` matches are React render-phase labels. This search supports traced command paths rather than proving facts about arbitrary third-party programs; commands and exact output are retained in `caller-firstparty-search.json`.
- Sandbox `/runs` accepts caller-selected argv (`tldw_Server_API/app/api/v1/endpoints/sandbox.py:1251-1355`). Execution defaults disabled (`app/core/config.py:1354`, `app/core/Sandbox/service.py:2048`). Host worktree preflight requires Git and unshare, accepts standard/trusted workloads, and rejects untrusted host-local workloads (`app/core/Sandbox/runners/worktree_runner.py:286-312`, `app/core/Sandbox/policy.py:204`). Linux execution wraps argv in **unshare --mount --pid --fork**, not nsenter, and launches without a privilege drop (`worktree_runner.py:432-453,554-577`). This is a real arbitrary-local-command path when enabled; it is not an automatic namespace-entry operation derived from a media request.
- Sandbox Docker commands act in a separately selected guest image. The runner always adds `--cap-drop ALL` and `--security-opt no-new-privileges:true`; optional SSH capabilities are only SYS_CHROOT/SETUID/SETGID (`docker_runner.py:330-342,564-601`). Docker `--mount` options are engine configuration, not calls to the matched application image's mount executable. These guest flags are not misattributed to the app container itself.
- ACP stdio can execute an arbitrary configured command (`app/core/Agent_Client_Protocol/stdio_client.py:78-96`), but registration is admin-only (`app/api/v1/endpoints/agent_client_protocol.py:2431-2460`). Prompt Studio host program execution requires explicit unsafe acknowledgement, plus a production acknowledgement in production (`app/core/Prompt_Management/prompt_studio/program_evaluator.py:85-95,123-153`). Neither path proves unprivileged local execution harmless. All relevant source excerpts and full-file hashes are retained in `caller-firstparty-excerpts.json`.

## Advisory-specific conclusions

[CVE-2026-53613](https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/security/advisories/GHSA-8gj5-72r3-428g) needs a privileged restricted mount authorized by a user/users fstab entry with an attacker-writable target ancestor. The verified frontend fstab and standalone Node caller paths supply neither authorization nor invocation. The four exact frontend rows support a current-use exception. Reopen if an operator adds the authorization and local execution, overrides fstab or installs a new privileged frontend handler. Non-root UID alone is not the rationale.

[CVE-2026-78408](https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/security/advisories/GHSA-55fx-f4gg-cfhj) requires privileged nsenter cgroup-v2 entry followed by execution of untrusted code with the retained writable cgroup descriptor. The package's 0755 nsenter does not create privilege itself. No current firstparty privileged caller performs that transition: the namespace wrapper is unshare. Three exact rows support only current firstparty-use exceptions; privileged operator nsenter commands, delegated cgroups and added wrappers are expressly outside that conclusion.

[CVE-2026-76642](https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/security/advisories/GHSA-m25x-3hj9-m26f) requires an executed filesystem helper failing nonzero and configured privileged idmap or owner/group/mode post-hooks. All five retained package inventories contain no installed filesystem mount helper. Exact backend source `libmount/src/context.c:2177-2243` searches the compiled FS_SEARCH_PATH; `configure.ac:2927-2952` defaults it to `/sbin:/sbin/fs.d:/sbin/fs`, with no Debian override found. Application uploads and PATH values are not a helper installation route. This is useful narrowing, but package inventory alone cannot certify all unowned backend base files or deployed overrides. Keep the six rows gated.

[CVE-2026-78410](https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/security/advisories/GHSA-rh77-686x-2f2m) requires restricted authorized bind/rbind use with attacker-replaceable source ancestors and X-mount.owner/group/mode. No structured API/job caller builds such an operation. Nevertheless, opt-in local program execution exists, the package ships setuid mount, and the actual backend/deployed authorizations have not been established. Keep the six rows gated.

For both backend mount families, **permission to run unprivileged local code is not permission to obtain root mount or metadata authority**. A claim that these are irrelevant because the user could already execute a program would erase the advisory's actual security boundary. A positive impact claim still needs an actual supported lower-privilege actor, invocation, relevant authorization/options/helper and replaceable path; none was confirmed here.

Supplementary GLib source inspection records table/monitor use in `gunixmounts.c` and the explicit mount subprocess in `gunixvolume.c:336-351`; no firstparty GVolume/Gio consumer was found. Those upstream files are not used as proof about exact Debian patch contents or as an absent-code exclusion. Their URLs/hashes are in `caller-glib-source.json` for the parent's separate review.
